title: Bhai Taru Singh on the Gurus’ Sacrifice for the Panth

blocks.text: Taru Singh answers the rescue proposal by declaring that he will not run from death when death has come through service to the Panth. For him, martyrdom is not an accident to avoid but a conscious offering that aligns his own fate with the path already shown by the Gurus.

He argues that the Gurus had given their own heads for the Panth, and not only their own heads but also the lives of sons and descendants. The point is not rhetorical excess: it grounds his refusal in a remembered chain of sacrifice through which Sikh dignity and collective purpose were preserved.

From that memory he draws a political lesson as well, namely that any hope of sovereignty or communal honor under Mughal oppression demands willingness to suffer rather than compromise. His answer turns personal arrest into a meditation on how the Panth grows through costly fidelity.
